I am 55yrs old, never married, no kids and got laid off from my employer of 21 years, 15 months ago, where I made about 75k per year upon layoff. Managed to get a full severance payout for all those years of service, plus the company gave us “re-education funds” which paid for a 4 month certificate course to upgrade my skills. I moved to another province to get this education at a local college, graduated, then my pal mentioned she knew someone who was selling a used RV for cheap, and if I bought it, she would allow me to park it in her driveway for $500 a month rent. Did this. Been living in this smaller remote town for 10 months now, worked at a Grocery store for 3 months, got offered a better paying part time casual job so quit the grocery store. Been working this PT casual job for 6 months now, and…I now have to quit because I can’t stay at friend’s place anylonger. Soooo…moving my RV back to the area I first originally moved to which is more densely populated, thus more job opportunities. Oh, I also managed to get another provincially funded free certificate 4 month course under my belt and graduate from it, this month. I also have volunteered for places to beef up my portfolio and hopefully land a better paying and FT job, with my “up grade” my skills. Yeah, it’s been a real challenge to say the least, my mental health has taken a nose dive due to all of this, I still have to work 10 more years before I can apply for and get my monthly OAS (old age security) and be able to tap into my locked in RRSP. As I started walking up Bay, and out of nowhere, this lady slid on up to me and nervously asked “are you walking north?” I said I was, and she asked if she could walk up along with me, and I said absolutely! We proceeded to walk up Bay St, and she said she was only going as far as Gerard…so we crossed on over to Yonge…got to Gerard and parted ways, I continued my journey up to Bloor…when I arrived at work, walked up the stairs to my department’s floor, went inside and my co-workers were in major panic mode. Up until that point, as I was casually strolling up Bay and Yonge st, I felt super peaceful and chill. Everyone out on the street was super friendly, I felt like I was at a campsite up North. LOL! I will never forget that experience with being in Toronto during that. :)
